title: Marginal cost analysis & staffing-mix scenarios
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a granular marginal cost model tied to staffing mix assumptions, and a small set of pricing-sensitivity scenarios for quick decisioning. Intended audience: Finance, GTM leads, and Product owners for Dedicated/Hosted pricing.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- We built a bottom-up marginal cost view that nests people costs (by role and allocation), infra (GPU hours, storage, egress), and fixed ops overhead into a per-million-token and per-embedding cost.
- Three scenarios (Base / Lean / Growth) show unit economics shifts under +/- 15% pricing delta and +/- 10% headcount mix changes.
- Key finding: a 10% shift from senior infra engineers to junior infra hires lowers short-term burn but increases marginal infra inefficiency leading to ~4-6% higher per-token costs in the first 6 months.

Assumptions (high level):
- Currency: USD; FY quarters align to calendar year quarters.
- FTE fully-loaded multiplier = base salary * 1.32 (benefits + payroll tax + office ops).
- Infra allocation: GPU hours allocated to 'hosted API' vs 'dedicated' based on current utilization trends (70/30 hosted/dedicated).
- Token baseline: 2.4B tokens/month (current run-rate across customers used for hosted pricing experiments).
- Embedding units baseline: 15M embeddings/month.

Key variables and shorthand used in tables:
- FTE_COST(role) = #headcount * average_base_salary(role) * 1.32
- MARGINAL_INFRA = reserved GPU amort (monthly) + burst credits + networking costs allocated to hosted flows
- UNIT_TOKENS = total tokens/month / 1,000,000 (we show per-million-token buckets)

Base inputs (snapshot used across scenarios):
- Roles and avg base salaries: Sr Infra Eng $220k, Infra Eng $150k, SRE $180k, Applied ML $190k, Product PM $160k, Sales AE $140k, CS Manager $140k
- Current headcount (allocated to product lines; hosted/dedicated/private split): Sr Infra Eng 6, Infra Eng 12, SRE 5, Applied ML 8, PM 4, Sales 10, CS 6
- Monthly infra amortization (reserved GPU cost + NVMe + network): $730,000
- Other monthly ops (licenses, office, support tools): $120,000

Representative calculation (Base case):
- Total monthly FTE cost = sum(FTE_COST(role)) = $1,982,400 (example calc, see sheet for per-role breakdown).
- Allocated to hosted products (70%) => $1,387,680.
- MARGINAL_COST_POOL = allocated FTE + infra amort ($730k*70%= $511k) + ops ($120k*70%= $84k) = $1,983,680 monthly.
- UNIT_TOKENS = 2,400 (2.4B tokens / 1M).
- Marginal cost per million tokens = MARGINAL_COST_POOL / UNIT_TOKENS = $826.53 per 1M tokens.

Scenario definitions (quick):
- Base: current headcount and utilization. End price target for hosted-generation: $1.35 per 1k tokens (=> $1,350 per 1M tokens).
- Lean: hiring freeze + rebalanced hiring (move hiring to IC infra roles only), -10% total FTE in Q1 ramp, small efficiency gains in infra (5%).
- Growth: aggressive sales & product spend to capture share, +12% FTE prioritized in sales & support in the next two quarters, infra capacity increased by 20% to avoid throttling.

Pricing sensitivity snapshot (per-million-token economics):
- We model price moves of -15%, -7.5%, 0%, +7.5%, +15% relative to the Base price. For each pricing move we calculate contribution margin with the Base marginal cost and for Lean/Growth adjusted marginal costs.

Mini table (rounded):
Scenario | Marginal cost per 1M | Base price per 1M | Contribution margin
Base     | $827                | $1,350             | 38.7%
Lean     | $790                | $1,350             | 41.5%
Growth   | $900                | $1,350             | 33.3%

Pricing sensitivity (selected cells):
- If price -15% (price = $1,147.5): Base margin => 27.9%; Lean => 31.6%; Growth => 19.7%
- If price +15% (price = $1,552.5): Base margin => 46.7%; Lean => 49.1%; Growth => 42.0%

Headcount plan (quarterly, condensed):
Columns: role | Q2 hires | Q3 hires | Q4 hires | Notes
Applied ML | 1 | 1 | 0 | focused on runtime quality and quantization
Infra Eng | 2 | 1 | 0 | one Sr hire backfill in Q2
Sr Infra Eng | 0 | 1 (backfill) | 0 | critical for kernel selection work
SRE | 0 | 0 | 1 | reliability focus for dedicated customers
Sales AE | 3 | 2 | 2 | growth scenario ramp in Q3
CS | 2 | 1 | 1 | onboarding for new dedicated accounts

Hiring triggers and stop-gaps (operational rules):
- Trigger 1 (price pressure): If 30-day revenue weighted median price across top-10 customers falls below 0.9 * target_price AND margin < 30% for > 2 consecutive weeks => temporary hiring freeze + reprioritize hiring toward efficiency roles (SRE, infra automation).
- Trigger 2 (capacity throttle): If 95th percentile latency SLO breaches and auto-scale costs > planned buffer for > 3 days => pause non-critical hiring and fund temporary burst capacity instead.
- Trigger 3 (growth unlock): If MRR net new from new logo wins > $250k for two consecutive months => enable +50% of planned sales hires for next quarter.

Operational levers to improve unit economics (short list):
- Improve prefix caching to reduce avg tokens/server-call by 9-12% (applied ML + infra effort).
- Shift 20% of low-latency but high-volume customers to a dedicated bundle with a higher committed price (negotiated discount vs on-demand).
- Introduce time-windowed pricing for embedding-heavy batch jobs (off-peak discounts).
- Quantization rollouts: estimate 7-11% infra cost savings once 4-bit variant reaches parity on key prompts.

Open questions / items for the spreadsheet that still need input:
- Precise per-role allocation splits between hosted/dedicated/private for newly hired PMs & applied ML (we used 70/20/10 as a proxy).
- Expected token growth rate for the next 9 months (we used conservative +2%/mo in Growth scenario).
- Actual negotiated GPU reserved pricing for next renewal cycle (we used list + 8% discount).

Next steps / asks:
- Finance: review per-role salary assumptions and confirm fully-loaded multiplier by 2026-03-10. (Assigned: Priya)
- Infra/Product: quantify caching delta by feature (work item tracked in JIRA-FEATURE-1198). Deliverable: delta estimates by 2026-03-20. (Assigned: Ethan)
- GTM: propose a dedicated-bundle price sheet (tiered committed thresholds + embedding add-on) by 2026-03-17. (Assigned: Olivia)

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This doc is intentionally calculation-heavy but still a working draft. The linked spreadsheet contains the per-role breakout and the sensitivity Monte Carlo tab. Please comment inline if you think a different baseline token run-rate is more representative.
- I left a couple of rough formulas in the sheet columns (see column H:J for role allocations). Be liberal with comments — we'll consolidate after the first pass.

Audit trail (edits):
- 2026-01-12: initial draft and first pass of role costs (Priya)
- 2026-02-02: infra amortization updated after negotiation with cloud partner (Marcus)
- 2026-03-05: added hiring triggers and growth scenario headcount (Olivia)

End of doc.
